title: A closed subscheme covered by effective Cartier divisors and a codimension two closed subset is, away from codimension two, an effective Cartier divisor supported on it
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if a closed subscheme Z of a Noetherian scheme is covered by integral effective Cartier divisors D_i together with a closed subset all of whose components have codimension at least two, then a nonnegative combination of the D_i is an effective Cartier divisor contained in Z and isomorphic to Z away from codimension two (statement lines 3075-3100). The counted proof is a genuine local argument: it defines the multiplicities a_i as valuations at the discrete valuation rings of the generic points, shows all but finitely many vanish, and then at an arbitrary point proves the delicate claim that the stalk of the ideal sheaf of Z is contained in the principal ideal generated by the product of the local equations of the relevant divisors, by an induction that peels off prime elements one at a time using that they are pairwise distinct (proof lines 3102-3143). It is H2: the arguments are carried out in full in the counted span and the only cited inputs are the discrete valuation ring property, local equations of Cartier divisors, and the UFD case used for the final existence sentence.
